research_rationale: EO 7759 (Revoking Executive Orders Nos. 7024-B and 7129-A; 2 FR 3097; approved Dec. 1, 1937) was read in full from the held Federal Register original. It is a single self-executing revocation of two earlier petroleum-shipment orders, so its one clause was exhausted on issue and the whole order is not in force on 2026-10-14. Status review: the order has no provisional status in the ledger; the status decision file for this member records the proposal 'no' on the order's own terms, and its one catalog observation (Revokes: EO 7024-B; EO 7129-A) concerns the targets, not this order. The held Office of the Federal Register note on EO 7759 lists Revokes: EO 7024-B and EO 7129-A, and See: EO 6979, EO 6980-C, EO 7757 and EO 7758; none of these entries says this order was amended, revoked or superseded, and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register catalog and saved order texts) found no later instrument that acts on EO 7759.
savings_reason: The order itself says the two revoked orders are superseded by Executive Order No. 7757 (Regulations Under the Act of February 22, 1935 As Amended by the Act of June 14, 1937) and Executive Order No. 7758 (Constituting Designated Area, and Establishing Federal Tender Board No. 1); the functions of the revoked orders were carried by those two orders and the revocation stands as an accrued result. The text of EO 7759 contains no savings clause for pending matters, so none is claimed beyond that transfer.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end is possible: the order's only command was performed when it was approved on December 1, 1937. The held catalog note for EO 7759 lists no instrument revoking, amending or superseding it; EO 6979, EO 6980-C, EO 7757 and EO 7758 appear in that note only as the earlier and companion orders the revocation concerns (the recitals tie EO 6979 and EO 6980-C to the agency and tender board that EO 7024-B created or relied on), not as events that act on EO 7759.
scope_check: The dossier inventory is one clause, 'whole', covering the sole operative paragraph. I read the held original text and confirm that it holds no other operative sentence: the two WHEREAS recitals describe EO 7024-B and EO 7129-A, and the NOW, THEREFORE paragraph is the only command.
independent_command_check: There is no independent command. The order revokes two named orders and names the two orders that replace them; it creates no new duty, authority, deadline or exception of its own.
savings_check: See the savings field: the revocation is an accrued result and the functions pass to EO 7757 and EO 7758, both of which the order names; no pending-matter saving clause is stated.

research_rationale: EO 8774 (Modifying Executive Order No. 8738 of April 21, 1941, Allocating by Types the Coffee Quota for Countries Not Signatories of the Inter-American Coffee Agreement; 6 FR 2845) was read in full from the held Federal Register original. It is a time-limited import permission tied to one quota year, so its sole clause ended by its own terms at the end of the quota year on September 30, 1941, and the whole order is not in force on 2026-10-14. The status decision for this member records 'no' on that own-terms ending. The single catalog observation (Amends: EO 8738, April 21, 1941) describes what this order did to another order; the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register catalog and saved order texts) found no later instrument acting on EO 8774.
savings_reason: EO 8774 contains no savings clause. Entries of coffee made during the quota year were completed acts under a permission that has expired, and no held source preserves any pending right, duty or proceeding under it after September 30, 1941.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for 'Executive Order No. 8738' and for 8774: the only later-looking hits are the order itself, its Federal Register printings, and the 1989 codification table entries described in the clause reason. EO 8814 (July 2, 1941) appears in that table as revoking EO 8773, not EO 8774. No revocation, supersession or earlier expiry of EO 8774 or EO 8738 before September 30, 1941 is held.
scope_check: One clause covers the sole operative paragraph and the effective-date sentence. The recitals state reasons only, and the footnote '6 F.R. 2047' is a citation. I confirmed there is no other operative text in the held original.
independent_command_check: The order has no independent command apart from the permission itself; it states that the mocha allocation of EO 8738 continues to apply and does not itself end or extend any other order.
savings_check: See the savings field: no savings clause and no held source of a pending matter.

research_rationale: EO 13374 (Amendments to Executive Order 12293, The Foreign Service of the United States; 70 FR 12961) was read in full from the held Federal Register original (two pages). Its three operative sections each perform one act on issue (two amendments of EO 12293 and the revocation of EO 13325), so every clause is spent on issue on 2005-03-14 and the order is not in force on 2026-10-14. The one machine current-law lead (CURRENT:EO:13374#0, 22 U.S.C. 3901 note) only lists this order among the orders that amended EO 12293; it shows the amended text living in the parent order, never this order in force, so it is not a current predicate. The three TERM records are wording leads taken from the replacement text that section 1 inserts into EO 12293 and describe that parent's salary classes, not a condition of this order. The Federal Register catalog note (Amends: EO 12293, February 23, 1981; Revokes: EO 13325, January 23, 2004) describes this order's own acts, and the bounded searches found no later instrument acting on EO 13374.
savings_reason: The text inserted by section 1 and the words substituted by section 2 became part of Executive Order 12293 as amended, which continues as a separate order; Executive Order 13325 stays revoked. The order itself has no savings clause for pending matters, so only the transfer of the new text into the parent order is claimed.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end exists because each act was performed on issue. I searched the held texts for the number 13374: only the order itself and its Federal Register print appear, and the catalog note and bounded searches list no revocation, supersession or amendment of EO 13374.
scope_check: The dossier splits the order into seven clauses (section 1 and its three pay-class items, section 2, section 3, section 4). I read the held original and confirm they cover every operative sentence; the three own-text records cover the amendment of section 4, the strike-and-insert of section 2 and the revocation of EO 13325, and the preamble recites authority and purpose only.
independent_command_check: The sections are separate acts: section 1 (new pay classes), section 2 (agency substitution) and section 3 (revocation of EO 13325) do not depend on one another; each is spent on issue. Section 4 is a rule of construction with no command.
savings_check: See the savings field. The amended provisions live on in EO 12293; no pending-matter savings clause is stated.

research_rationale: EO 13646 (Establishing the President's Advisory Council on Financial Capability for Young Americans; 78 FR 39159) was read in full from the held Federal Register original. It establishes an advisory Council within the Department of the Treasury and, in section 6, ends it 2 years after the order's date unless the President extends it. No extension is held, so every clause ended by the order's own terms on June 25, 2015, and the whole order has no operative force on 2026-10-14. The U.S. Code lead (CURRENT:EO:13646#0, 20 U.S.C. 9701 note) only prints the order as a note with no ending statement; a printed note does not show the Council continuing, and I did not treat it as a current predicate. The catalog observation for EO 13646 has an empty note, which establishes nothing about current effect; the status decision records 'no' on the order's own terms and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register catalog and saved order texts), which found no later instrument acting on EO 13646.
savings_reason: EO 13646 contains no savings clause for the Council's work after termination. Its section 7 only preserves the authority of departments and the functions of the Office of Management and Budget, which exist independently of the order, and no held source preserves any duty, right or proceeding under the order after June 25, 2015.
earlier_end_check: The order has a fixed term, so the question is whether anything ended it before June 25, 2015 or extended it. I searched the held texts for the order's number and the Council's name: only the order and the June 2015 Treasury notice appear (the notice shows the Council still meeting on June 17, 2015, so no end before that meeting). No instrument revoking or amending EO 13646 is held, and the catalog note is empty.
scope_check: The dossier splits the order into 41 clauses covering sections 1 to 7 and their subparts; the machine labels with a 'dup' suffix are the second and third items numbered (i) and (ii) under sections 3(f), 4(b) and 4(c). I read the held original from the title to the signature and confirm that no operative sentence is missing; the sections run from char 884 to 9967 of the held text.
independent_command_check: There is no command independent of the Council: every section either establishes, staffs, directs or funds the Council, qualifies the order's implementation, or states the policy the Council exists to implement. Section 6 supplies the one end for all of them.
savings_check: See the savings field: no savings clause and no held source of a surviving right or duty.

research_rationale: EO 13244 (Providing an Order of Succession Within the Department of the Interior; 66 FR 66267, December 21, 2001) was read in full from the held Federal Register original. It sets a standing order of succession for the Secretary of the Interior. It was amended once (EO 13261, March 19, 2002, section 3(a) only) and was expressly revoked in its entirety by section 4 of EO 13915 (April 14, 2020; 85 FR 21733), whose text is held; EO 13915 then re-issues a similar succession order of its own. No held source shows an earlier end. The catalog note (Revokes: EO 11487; Amended by: EO 13261; Revoked by: EO 13915), the held 5 U.S.C. 3345 note and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register catalog and saved order texts) agree. The status decision records 'no': the order was formally revoked and has no operative force on 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: Executive Order 13915, whose sections 1 to 3 restate the succession rule, the list of officers (with one more office added) and the exceptions, replaced EO 13244 and carries the same standing rule forward. EO 13915 section 4 revokes EO 13244 without a savings clause, and the held text does not preserve any pending action under EO 13244 beyond that replacement.
earlier_end_check: I searched the held corpus for the number 13244: the hits are the order itself, EO 13261 (amends section 3(a), and the same amendment lists in the U.S. Code note), EO 13915 (revokes it), and the Federal Register prints of those orders. The order has no sunset, condition or fixed term in its text. The three TERM records are wording leads from section 1's contingency (the Secretary and Deputy Secretary unable to act), a recurring condition and not an end. The one earlier ending is section 4's revocation of EO 11487, which was performed on signing.

The 11 clauses are the preamble, sections 1 and 4, subsections 2(a)-(f) and 3(a)-(b); I read the held original and confirm they cover every operative sentence. The amendment of EO 13261 reaches only section 3(a). The revocation in EO 13915 section 4 is whole-order.
independent_command_check: Section 4 (revocation of EO 11487) is an independent one-time command and ended on issue; the succession rule and its exceptions are one standing rule that ended together on April 14, 2020. The reservation of presidential discretion in section 3(b) does not outlive the rule it qualifies.
